title: Lick Skillet Road on the battlefield
text: Reports from the Battle of Ezra Church name Lick Skillet Road, leading west to the crossroads settlement later called Adamsville.

title: Lick Skillet becomes Adamsville
text: Renamed after the Adams Lodge, a Masonic order founded by George W. Adams; the name becomes official in 1906.

title: A school for Black children
text: Bethlehem Church School opens, the first school for African American students in Adamsville-Boulder Park; later L. P. Miles Elementary.

title: Margaret Fain School built
text: Becomes the community's meeting hall, cafeteria and playground for decades.

title: Population 1176
text: The Adamsville district is still sparsely settled.

title: Train wreck near Adamsville
text: A photographer documents an Atlantic Birmingham & Coast Line wreck near the settlement.

title: Annexed by Atlanta
text: The Civic Club dates its annexation to 1951, the year the Plan of Improvement passed; Atlanta tripled in area in 1952.

title: Residents write their own plan
text: The Adamsville Civic Club, with planner Leon S. Eplan, publishes Neighborhood Planning in Adamsville: Now... Tomorrow.

title: The expressway as a color line
text: A city Report on the Adamsville Transition Area acknowledges the planned west expressway as a white/Black boundary.

title: Barricade in nearby Cascade Heights
text: Mayor Ivan Allen Jr. blocks Peyton Road after white residents demand a racial buffer; a court orders it removed after 72 days.

title: Annexation referendum
text: State law authorizes a vote to annex the remaining unincorporated Adamsville area, effective January 1, 1967.

title: I-20 and I-285 meet at Adamsville
text: The interstate exit takes the neighborhood's name.

title: West Adamsville: Ultimate Development
text: City map plans a shopping center at Gordon and Fairburn and an expanded Wilson Mill Park.
source: Atlanta Department of Budget and Planning (1970)

title: MARTA's west line promise
text: A West Line extension toward Fulton Industrial Boulevard enters MARTA's long-range plan with the 1971 referendum.

title: NPU system created
text: Under Mayor Maynard Jackson and planning commissioner Leon Eplan, Atlanta creates Neighborhood Planning Units.

title: NPU-H Five Year Plan
text: The first NPU-H land-use plan maps Adamsville with Boulder Park, Fairburn Heights and Carroll Heights.

title: C. T. Martin elected
text: Serves District 10 for nearly 30 years and pushes a new recreation center onto the site of a troubled apartment complex.

title: West Line study reopens
text: MARTA studies rail or bus rapid transit from H. E. Holmes to Fulton Industrial; 98 percent of surveyed riders support it. It is still not built.

title: Hollowell/MLK TAD created
text: Tax increment district covering the MLK corridor; lists Adamsville Village as a site.

title: NPU-H Master Plan
text: Goals include aging in place, engaging renters and healthy food access.

title: Fain building becomes a ninth-grade campus
text: About 300 Douglass High freshmen move into the old Fain school.

title: Adamsville Legacy mural
text: Artist Ashley Dopson paints local leaders on MLK Jr. Dr.; Mayor Dickens: I grew up right here.

title: Free food center opens
text: Atlanta Community Food Bank opens in a former Family Dollar at the crossroads.

title: APS plans to close the ninth-grade building
text: Part of a plan to close or repurpose 16 schools.

title: Residents describe what is still missing
text: Interviews name food, sidewalks, flooding, safety and participation.
